rationale:
OWNER DECISION 4, 2026-08-18, on bugs_open/300: 'as recommended — resolve by (page_id, slot_name), id as tiebreak'.

THE PROBLEM, plainly. The page_component_status_drift discovery check stores `page_components.id` as its finding's only handle on the subject. The estate's own rule says that id is not stable across re-renders — written in 016b ('Do not key re-validation on a stored component_id … Key on (page_name, slot_name)') and obeyed by two live call sites that say so in their comments (revalidate_review_queue_action.go:648, create_report_page_action.go:21). So an ordinary re-render between filing and dispatch turns a TRUE finding into sql.ErrNoRows, which fixPageComponentStatus turns into a hard error, which makes the work item `failed`.

WHY THAT COSTS MORE THAN ONE LOST REPAIR. detected-item-promoter's floor (migrations 444/454) holds any (item_type, handler_agent) pair under 25% success over >=5 terminal outcomes, and it counts `failed`. A dead subject id is indistinguishable, to that gate, from a handler that cannot do its job. The compounding path is: a finding waits, its page is re-rendered, its id dies, it dispatches, it fails, the ratio falls, and the promoter stops dispatching page_component_status_drift ENTIRELY — including the findings that are still true. The type disables itself by ageing, and the symptom points at the wrong component. The pair's lifetime record is 4 complete / 0 failed; five id-rot failures put it under the floor.

THE MEASUREMENT, which could have come out otherwise and did not. [MEASURED 2026-08-18, all 82 lifetime rows] every row carries `page_id` and `spec.slot_name`. `spec.page_component_id` resolves for 70 of 82 — **12 dead ids already, 15%**. `(page_id, slot_name)` resolves for **82 of 82**. And the ageing is observed rather than predicted: the bug file recorded on 2026-08-17 that all 16 deferred rows' ids still resolved; today 11 do. Five died in a day, in a queue nobody touched.

WHY THE TIEBREAK IS NOT DECORATION, which is the part I would push on if I were reviewing. `(page_id, slot_name)` is NOT unique. [MEASURED 2026-08-18] 17 (page_id, slot_name) pairs on the estate carry more than one component, worst case 4. Zero of them are drift rows today — which is exactly the trap: resolving by the pair alone is correct on every row that exists now and silently wrong on the first one that is not, and no test written against today's data would catch it. So the stored id wins WITHIN the pair's matches when it is still alive; a lone match is taken; and genuine ambiguity is REFUSED rather than guessed, in the same posture as the two guards already in this function.

WHY IT JOINS THROUGH work_item_id RATHER THAN READING page_id. [VERIFIED 2026-08-18 against build-dispatch-loop's live sub_workflow] the call_handler input_mapping does carry `page_id?` — correcting this lane's own earlier claim that it does not — but the `?` makes it optional, so it is omitted whenever the row's page_id is NULL (a sampled live component-template-fixer payload had no page_id for exactly that reason). `work_item_id` is unconditionally mapped, and site_work_items.page_id is a real column, so joining through it cannot be broken by a change to an optional mapping entry and needs no change to the shared dispatch config that every handler reads.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. If BOTH keys miss — the page itself is gone — it is still a hard error and still reaches the floor. That is candidate 1 as approved; softening a genuinely-missing subject is a different judgement about what `complete` means on this handler, and it is stated as a residual rather than quietly widened.

plan.summary: fixPageComponentStatus resolves its subject by the unstable page_components.id alone and returns a hard error when it misses, so a finding that ages past a re-render becomes a `failed` work item and a vote against its (item_type, handler_agent) pair in detected-item-promoter's 25% floor. This adds resolveStatusRepairComponent: resolve by the stable (page_id, slot_name) — reached by joining site_work_items through the unconditionally-mapped work_item_id — with the stored id as the tiebreak when that pair is ambiguous (17 such pairs exist fleet-wide), a refusal rather than a guess when it is ambiguous and the stored id is not among the matches, and a fallback to the stored id when the pair yields nothing so every existing caller is unchanged. Every outcome now records `resolved_by` so a census can tell which key did the work. Measured: the stored id resolves for 70 of 82 lifetime rows, the stable pair for 82 of 82.

edits.rationale: The resolver. Prefers the stable key, breaks an ambiguous pair with the stored id, refuses rather than guesses when it cannot, and falls back to the stored id so nothing that worked before changes. Fails OPEN to the stored id on a lookup error — a new query must not be able to make the action worse than the behaviour it replaces. Returns `resolvedBy` so the choice is auditable on the row rather than only in a log.

Route the lookup through the resolver, and make an unidentifiable subject a SOFT refusal (fixed:false, action:needs_review) rather than a hard error — matching the three guards already in this function and keeping an artefact problem off the promoter's failure ledger. The subsequent page_components load is unchanged; it now runs against the resolved id, and pcIDStr is re-pointed at it so the result names what was actually inspected.

edits.rationale: Seven cases, and the fallback ones are the load-bearing half: without them 'the stable key is used' is equally consistent with having broken every other caller of this fix_type. Mutation-proven before submitting — stable key never consulted -> 4 RED; tiebreak removed so an ambiguous pair takes the first match -> 2 RED; fallback removed -> 2 RED. The ambiguity tests are written against a population that has ZERO ambiguous drift rows today, deliberately: that is the case no query on current data would catch.

plan.risks:
1. **The soft refusal completes the item.** component-template-fixer's workflow branches only on `fix_result.fixed == true`, so a `fixed:false` return still ends in complete_workflow and the dispatch loop marks the item `complete` — the same as this function's three existing needs_review arms. So an ambiguous slot is recorded as handled with the reason on the row, not left open. A reviewer should say whether that is right or whether it should be needs_human_review; I kept the function's existing semantics rather than inventing a new one inside a bug patch.

2. **Both keys missing is still a hard error**, and still feeds the floor. Stated as a residual, not fixed: candidate 1 is what was approved and this is a different judgement.

3. **One extra query per repair_page_component_status call.** This fix_type is low-volume (82 lifetime rows). The lookup fails OPEN to the stored id, so a query error cannot make the action worse than before.

4. **The join assumes the work item row still exists** when the handler runs. It does — the loop claims it, and it is the row being completed — but if a future caller invokes this fix_type without a work_item_id it falls back to the stored id, which is exactly the old behaviour.

5. **What a reviewer should check that I could not:** whether any OTHER fix_type in this action keys on a stored page_components.id the same way. I read the two neighbours (align_slot_name uses the id it was given for an UPDATE, same exposure) and did not widen the change to them, because a shared-mechanism change inside a bug patch is what the 2026-07-28 ruling vetoes. If the seat thinks align_slot_name should move too, say so and it becomes its own round.
